messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: us-west-2 runtime latency anomaly. In-flight > 1200, queue latency spike for 18m. Paging oncall.

oncall_maya: grabbing state. seeing a big uptick on embedding and chat-gen tail latencies. p95 up 3x. probable root: a scheduled batch push from partner X + spike in streaming chat sessions.

eng_jay: can you dump top tenants and current runtime knobs? I have a shortlist of mitigations (lower max_inflight, enable tenant shedding, disable experimental fast_stream for non-premium).

oncall_maya: cluster snapshot: 
```
max_inflight_total: 4000
max_inflight_per_worker: 25
per_tenant_token_bucket: enabled
fast_stream_feature: true
request_timeout_sec: 45
queue_limit_pct: 85
```
Top traffic: partner-x (42%), cust-D (15%), cust-E (9%), health-check-batcher (8%).

cs_mike: note cust-D is on SLA and we get alerted for any >10% degradation. cust-E is self-serve; lower tolerance. We'll need targeted exemptions.

oncall_maya: immediate actions I propose:
- set `max_inflight_total` -> 3200 to force soft shedding across pool
- reduce `max_inflight_per_worker` -> 12 to reduce contention
- add per-tenant shed rule: drop batched requests > 10k tokens unless premium
- disable `fast_stream_feature` on /v1/chat/stream for non-premium to avoid head-of-line blocking
- create temporary per-tenant token-bucket limits for health-check-batcher to 1 qps

eng_jay: I'm going to push the quick changes now. running: 
```
redwoodctl runtime set-config --cluster us-west-2 --key max_inflight_total --value 3200 --reason "emergency-shed"
redwoodctl runtime set-config --cluster us-west-2 --key max_inflight_per_worker --value 12
```

infra-bot: config-change accepted: max_inflight_total=3200 at 4292005568; max_inflight_per_worker=12 at 4292005570. Triggering rolling worker recycle (graceful).

eng_jay: recycle progressing; 60% of workers rotated. queues down ~22% already. p95 for embeddings trending down. some batched jobs still hit tail.

oncall_maya: applying tenant shedding and fast_stream toggle for non-premium now.
```
redwoodctl ratelimit add-tenant-rule --tenant health-check-batcher --max-qps 1 --priority high
redwoodctl runtime feature-toggle set --feature fast_stream_feature --route /v1/chat/stream --scope non-premium --value false
redwoodctl policy add --name batched-token-shed --condition "tokens>10000 and not premium" --action drop
```

infra-bot: tenant-rule created at 4292005582. feature-toggle applied at 4292005585. policy batched-token-shed accepted at 4292005588.

product_charlie: FYI the partner-x batch job is expected till end of day; we should consider moving them to a dedicated pool tomorow. Logging CS and partner success contact.

cs_mike: I've messaged cust-D and cust-E about potential short throttling windows. cust-D flagged as high priority.

sre_sam: seeing reduced contention on KV cache and fewer worker retries. however, retries from non-premium clients increased slightly due to dropping large batches. we might need to add a short-backoff advisory in the error response to reduce retry storms.

eng_jay: good point. adding a 5s Retry-After header for dropped responses now and setting client-facing error code 429 with body explaining temporary shedding.
```
redwoodctl response-template update --code 429 --body "Temporary capacity shedding. Retry-After: 5" --cluster us-west-2
```

infra-bot: response-template updated at 4292005596.

oncall_maya: After changes: queue depth down ~58%, p95 embeddings dropped to 1.8x baseline, overall error rate up 0.6 percentage points (mostly 429s).

eng_jay: Plan for next steps: if stable for 12m and p95 under threshold, incrementally restore max_inflight_total by +300 every 5m until baseline. Do not re-enable fast_stream for non-premium until partner-X moved or batcher is rate-limited.

product_charlie: I'll schedule partner-X cutover to dedicated pool in morning runbook. Also request feature gating to offer batch-friendly endpoints for large jobs.

cs_mike: customers informed. No active escalations, but cust-D asked for a post-incident call if they see degraded throughput.

sre_sam: I'm going to watch for retry amplification. if we see spike in retry rates, we'll tighten per-tenant token bucket and bump request_timeout to 60 to reduce client-side quick retries.

oncall_maya: handoff: @oncall_maya -> @oncall-next-lee will take shift at 14:30. leaving notes in incident doc and runbook: /incidents/4292005555-traffic-shepherding-runtime. pager: paging oncall-next-lee now.

incident-bot: PAGED: oncall-next-lee at 4292005602 for handoff.

oncall-next-lee: acked. joining in 5. thanks for the detailed notes.

eng_jay: stable window reached at 4292005650. starting staged restore: set max_inflight_total=3500.

infra-bot: max_inflight_total updated to 3500 at 4292005655.

eng_jay: monitoring... stable for 8m. will leave staged restore queued. handover to oncall-next-lee in 10.

oncall-next-lee: taking over. I'll keep watch for retry amplification and customer impact. cs_mike keep me posted if cust-D reports anything.

cs_mike: will do. opening follow-up ticket for post-incident review and communication draft.

oncall-next-lee: closing active mitigation loop and capturing action items: partner-X to dedicated pool, add batch-friendly endpoint, metric alert refinement for batchers, consider adaptive token-bucket per-tenant.

incident-bot: incident doc updated at 4292005779. incident status: mitigated, monitoring.
